subject: MSA / Order Form: integrate security addendum and breach sub-limit
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: security addendum linkage for breach cap

Hi Monica,

Thanks for moving quickly on the MSA. Procurement asked that we explicitly tie the breach-specific liability sub-limit to the Security Addendum rather than burying the language in the general MSA caps. Attached is our current redline and a short note from procurement.

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm a reasonable sub-limit for data security incidents (they proposed $250k but want to understand Redwood's position).
- Make sure carve-outs for consequential damages remain intact but that security incidents are carved out to the sub-limit in the Addendum.
- We need a requirement for an independent forensic report to trigger certain remedies.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept linkage to the Security Addendum and propose language we can circulate back to procurement?

Attachment: Acme_MSA_redline.docx (docx)

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Head of Procurement
Acme Health
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: security addendum linkage for breach cap

Samantha,

Appreciate the context and the redline. Quick thoughts from legal/sales side:

- We are ok tying the breach sub-limit to the Security Addendum, provided the Addendum contains a clear definition of "security incident" and the triggers for remedial obligations.
- On quantum: $250k is below our typical risk tolerance for enterprise customers at this spend band. Our usual asks are either a fixed sub-limit around $500k or a percentage-based floor (e.g., 10-15% of ARR or prior 12-month invoiced spend), whichever is higher.
- Carve-outs: we need to keep gross negligence and willful misconduct carved out of the limitation, but will accept the Addendum to govern breach-specific allocation.
- Forensics: we can require an independent forensic report within 30 days of discovery to qualify for certain remedies; we should narrow the scope so it doesn't become automatic "admission of liability".

I'm attaching our proposed redline for the Security Addendum. If procurement can agree to a sub-limit formula (fixed floor + % of spend) we can update the Order Form to reflect the waterfall: Order Form cap -> Security sub-limit -> carve-outs as listed.

Attachment: Security_Addendum_v2.docx (docx)

Next steps: Lauren, Ben — can you confirm commercial impact if we set sub-limit floor at $500k vs $250k (Ben) and whether pricing needs an amendment (Lauren)? Samantha — if you can confirm which metric procurement prefers for the percentage (ARR vs trailing 12 months spend) we can finalize.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Miles Carter <miles.carter@lawfirmb.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: security addendum linkage for breach cap

Monica / Samantha —

Quick read-through from outside counsel. I put tracked changes into the Security Addendum and flagged one structural issue: linking the sub-limit to the Addendum is fine, but the Addendum needs to reference the Order Form value calculation explicitly to avoid disputes. Two practical approaches:

1) Fixed floor approach: security sub-limit = greater of $500,000 or 15% of the then-current Order Form value; or
2) Spend-based approach: security sub-limit = greater of $500,000 or 10% of the trailing 12 months invoice amount under the Agreement.

My recommendation is (1) for speed (clear and predictable) but (2) is better for long-term alignment with commercial consumption models. Also suggested:
- Add a discovery/notification timeline (48 hours initial notification, full incident report within 30 days).
- Require a mutually agreed forensic vendor or allow Redwood to propose one subject to Acme's approval (not unreasonably withheld).
- Carve-outs: preserve gross negligence/willful misconduct; exclude from limitation any regulatory fines/penalties that cannot be contractually limited by law.

Attachment: Security_Addendum_v3.docx (docx)

Happy to hop on a short call if you want to finalize language.

—Miles Carter
Partner, LawFirm B
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Miles Carter <miles.carter@lawfirmb.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: security addendum linkage for breach cap

Thanks Miles — helpful options.

We propose the following compromise to move procurement along:
- Security sub-limit = greater of $500,000 or 10% of trailing 12 months billed amount under the Order Form;
- Forensic report requirement: independent forensic report within 30 days to unlock certain remediation credits; Redwood to propose vendor if Acme does not nominate one within 7 days;
- Continue to preserve carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct; regulatory fines excluded to the extent not contractually limitable;
- Add a mutual cooperation clause and explicit tie-back sentence in the Order Form: "For the avoidance of doubt, the security sub-limit described in the Security Addendum is the exclusive remedy for data security incidents as set forth therein, subject to the carve-outs listed."

Aditya — FYI on the proposed floor/percent. If procurement accepts the formula above we will not ask for price increases, but this is a commercial trade (Ben / Lauren please confirm internal acceptance).

If Acme can sign off in principle we will produce a final redline and pull a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Thanks,
Monica
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, Miles Carter <miles.carter@lawfirmb.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: security addendum linkage for breach cap

Monica —

This looks reasonable. Procurement will take the proposed compromise to leadership this morning (floor + 10% trailing 12 months). They asked for two small clarifications:
1) Include explicit wording that the forensic report "does not constitute an admission of liability";
2) Add a requirement that Redwood provides the SOC2 report referenced in the Addendum within five business days of request.

Please circulate the final redline and we will process via DocuSign. Attaching current Order Form and Acme's latest SOC2 snapshot for reference.

Attachments: Order_Form_ACME_v2.pdf (pdf); SOC2_Report_ACME_2026.pdf (pdf)

DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/transactions/ABC12345

Thanks — will confirm once procurement approves.

Best,
Samantha

Acme Health
